seoTitle: Young Sheldon Test: Which Character Are You? (12 Questions)
metaDescription: Take the Young Sheldon test: 12 everyday questions reveal whether you're Sheldon, Mary, George, Georgie, Missy, Meemaw or Mandy — with your full character breakdown.
intro: Are you the genius, the hustler, or the one with a deck of cards? Answer 12 everyday questions about family, money and getting by, and find out which Young Sheldon character you are.

characters.name: Sheldon Cooper
characters.title: The Boy Genius
characters.summary: Brilliant, rule-bound and completely honest. You know exactly how things should be done, and you'll happily explain it.
description: Like Sheldon, you're usually the smartest person in the room. He's a child prodigy who joins his older brother Georgie's high school class at just nine.
You love what you love. Sheldon is obsessed with science, trains, comic books and Spock from Star Trek.
You aim high. Sheldon starts college at East Texas Tech at 11, graduates at 14 and heads off to Caltech.
characters.flaw: You say exactly what you think, even when nobody asked.
characters.signature: A strict schedule, a head full of facts and an opinion on everything.
characters.clashReason: they'd correct you in front of everyone, and they'd be right

characters.name: Mary Cooper
characters.title: The Protective Mom
characters.summary: Loving, devoted and fierce when it counts. You'd do anything for your family, whether they like it or not.
description: Like Mary, you'd do anything for your family. She's a loving, overprotective mother, and she worries about Sheldon most of all.
Faith matters to you. Mary is a devout Southern Baptist, and she takes a job as the secretary at her church.
You don't hold back. Mary has a short temper and a sharp tongue, but she's kind at heart.
characters.flaw: You worry so much that you smother the people you love.
characters.signature: A Bible by the bed, dinner on the table and a worried look.
characters.clashReason: they'd tell you how to live your life, for your own good

characters.name: George Cooper Sr.
characters.title: The Tired Dad
characters.summary: Easygoing, hard-working and quietly loyal. You'd rather keep the peace than make a fuss.
description: Like George, you work hard for the people you love. He's the head football coach at Medford High.
You don't always say how you feel. George is easygoing on the surface, and he tries his best with a son who's nothing like him.
You dream big, quietly. Late in the series, George is offered his dream job coaching college football at Rice University.
characters.flaw: You'd rather keep the peace than say what's really bothering you.
characters.signature: A whistle round your neck, a long day behind you and the game on TV.
characters.clashReason: they'd shrug and say 'leave it' when you wanted to talk it out

characters.name: Georgie Cooper
characters.title: The Hustler
characters.summary: Street-smart, charming and always working an angle. You may not love school, but you understand money.
description: Like Georgie, you've always got a money-making plan. He's laid-back about school but sharp whenever there's cash involved.
You start working early. Georgie gets a job at the sports store run by Meemaw's boyfriend, Dale.
You step up when it counts. When Mandy, who's older than him, gets pregnant, Georgie decides to marry her, and they name their daughter CeeCee after Meemaw.
characters.flaw: You're always one scheme away from trouble.
characters.signature: A side hustle, a smooth line and cash in your back pocket.
characters.clashReason: they'd try to sell you something you didn't need

characters.name: Missy Cooper
characters.title: The Overlooked Twin
characters.summary: Sharp, sarcastic and great with people. You notice everything, especially when you're being ignored.
description: Like Missy, you read people better than anyone. She's Sheldon's twin, and her social skills are far better than his.
You're tougher than you look. Missy joins the town's baseball team.
You won't be ignored. Fed up with her parents always putting Sheldon first, Missy packs a bag, takes her dad's pickup and runs away in the middle of the night.
characters.flaw: You keep score of every time someone else got the attention.
characters.signature: A sarcastic comeback, an eye-roll and a baseball glove.
characters.clashReason: they'd roll their eyes and say what everyone else was thinking

characters.name: Meemaw
characters.title: The Free Spirit
characters.summary: Fun, bold and nobody's idea of a sweet little grandma. You live life on your own terms.
description: Like Meemaw, you live life on your own terms. She's Sheldon's free-spirited, outspoken grandmother, and she lives right nearby.
You like a bit of risk. Meemaw loves to gamble, and she even runs an illegal casino in the back room of the laundromat she buys.
You're a softie underneath. Meemaw calls Sheldon "Moonpie," and he's sure he's her favorite grandchild.
characters.flaw: You'd rather take the risk than think about what happens next.
characters.signature: A deck of cards, a quick comeback and a date on Saturday night.
characters.clashReason: they'd talk you into a bet you were always going to lose

characters.name: Mandy McAllister
characters.title: The Grown-Up
characters.summary: Grounded, independent and honest. You've seen a bit of life, and you don't need anyone's permission.
description: Like Mandy, you've seen a bit of life. She's more than ten years older than Georgie, and their fling leads to a baby.
You can stand on your own. When Mandy finds out she's pregnant, she first plans to raise the baby by herself.
You want something for yourself too. Soon after CeeCee is born, Mandy goes for a job as the local TV weather girl.
characters.flaw: You keep people at arm's length until they've proved themselves.
characters.signature: A clear head, a straight answer and a plan B.
characters.clashReason: they'd tell you to grow up, and they'd mean it

questions.text: A neighbor invites you to a backyard barbecue. You...

options.text: Help the host, and keep an eye on who's drinking too much
Grab a cold drink and find whoever's talking football
Work out which guests are worth getting to know
Ask exactly how long you're expected to stay

questions.text: Your phone bill is much higher than usual. You...

options.text: Go through it line by line until you find the mistake
Call them up and talk your way into a discount
Pay it, and grumble about it all evening
Laugh it off. Money comes and goes

questions.text: You have a whole Saturday with nothing planned. You spend it...

options.text: Sleeping in, then the game on TV with nobody needing anything
On a road trip with friends, in no hurry to get home
Getting the house in order, then cooking a big family dinner
At the mall with friends, catching up on all the gossip

questions.text: A friend asks you to keep a big secret. You...

options.text: Warn them you're terrible at keeping secrets
Promise you will, then quietly start worrying about them
Agree, then ask what they're actually going to do about it
Keep it, and never bring it up again

questions.text: A coworker presents your idea in a meeting as if it were theirs. You...

options.text: Correct them on the spot, in detail, in front of everyone
Smile, say nothing and get even later
Pull them aside and calmly tell them you noticed
Let it slide. It's not worth the fight

questions.text: A friend says you should take up a new hobby. You...

options.text: Say thanks, but you like your evenings exactly as they are
Try dance lessons. You might meet someone
Start a side hustle instead. Hobbies don't pay
Join something at church, so it does some good

questions.text: A family member makes a decision you think is a big mistake. You...

options.text: Keep telling them until they change their mind
Tell them once, honestly, then let them get on with it
Remind them you made worse ones and turned out fine
Stay out of it, and get ready to say 'I told you so'

questions.text: At a family dinner, everyone's talking about someone else's big news. You...

options.text: Join in. You're proud of them
Point out, sarcastically, that you're here too
Wait for a gap, then change the subject to something interesting
Eat, nod along and slip off early

questions.text: You win $500 in a raffle. You...

options.text: Put it straight into something that'll make more
Head to the casino. You're feeling lucky
Put it toward something the family actually needs
Treat yourself to one nice thing, then save the rest

questions.text: A new person joins your group of friends. You...

options.text: Work out within five minutes whether they're trouble
Make them laugh, and have them feeling at home by the end of the night
Be friendly, but make up your mind about them in your own time
Nod hello and let them come to you

questions.text: You're raising three very different kids in a small Texas town, and one of them is a genius. You...

options.text: Pray on it, and protect that child from the world
Make sure the other two get some attention too
Let them all be who they are, and spoil them on weekends
Take it one day at a time. Nobody gets a manual

questions.text: Your family runs a little shop in a small town, and business is bad. You...

options.text: Open a back room for card games. What's the harm?
Work every hour you can to keep it going
Draw up a proper business plan, with charts
Make it clear you're not giving up your weekends for it
